# DSP Architecture: O-GranulatorInstrument

**CRITICAL CONTRACT:** This specification is immutable during Stages 1-4 implementation. Stage 1 cannot proceed without this file. Stage 2 (DSP) implements this exact architecture.

**Generated by:** Stage 0 Research (research-planning-agent, 2026-11-07)
**Referenced by:** Stage 1 (Foundation), Stage 2 (DSP), Stage 3 (GUI), Stage 4 (Polish)
**Complexity tier:** 6 (file I/O + off-thread decode/swap, polyphonic MIDI/MPE synth, per-voice grain clouds, feedback into working copies, live per-voice grain visualisation)
**Research depth:** DEEP
**JUCE:** 8.0.15 (local `/Users/taylorbrook/JUCE/modules`; APIs verified by header grep, NE patch marker present)
**Parent:** `plugins/O-Granulator` @ `3043b72a` (Stage 3, phase 3.3 planned). Its `research/ARCHITECTURE.md` is referenced by section (`GR-ARCH §N`) and is NOT re-documented here.
**Substrate:** `modules/synthesis/grain-engine` v1.1.0, `modules/tuning/pitch-collections` v1.0.0, `modules/effects/reverb-unit` 1.2.0 (atomic bind, as used by the parent), `modules/tuning/note-expression` v1.1.1, `modules/core/webview-drop-streaming` v1.0.0, `modules/persistence/preset-manager`.

**Contract inputs:** BRIEF.md, REQUIREMENTS.md (24 reqs), parameter-spec-draft.md (261 params, 6 open questions). No mockup yet. The full `parameter-spec.md` comes from the mockup and is required before Stage 1. Parameter changes from this document are listed under **Design Sync** at the end. The draft itself is not edited.

## Stage 0 Decisions (the 7 questions)

| # | Question | Decision | Section |
|---|----------|----------|---------|
| D1 | Share the O-Granulator core as a module, or fork it | **Fork at leaf granularity now; converge into grain-engine 1.2.0 after O-Granulator ships.** The parent `Engine` (1659 + 750 lines) is shaped around one live ring, one loop and global streams, so it cannot be shared. Its leaves (GrainFx, WindowMorphBank, OutputLaw, Quotas, ScaleQuantiser, FeedbackChain, TempoTracker, ControlGrid ramps) are copied verbatim, under a provenance manifest with a per-file sha256. The fork happens at the start of Phase 2.1, pinned to the O-Granulator commit that closes 3.3. | Arch Decisions §A1 |
| D2 | Max slot length / rate, memory | **30 s per slot, with a hard cap of 2,880,000 frames (30 s up to 96 kHz, 15 s at 192 kHz).** The working tape is held at session rate with 4 mip levels (float, ×1.9375). The pristine copy is held at the file's native rate, level 0 only. Memory is allocated per loaded length, not reserved. Four full slots take about 135 MB at 48 k and about 225 MB at 96 k, plus ≤ 1 tape build and the capture buffer in flight. | §5, §7, Special Considerations |
| D3 | CPU at 16 voices × 4 streams; grain_limit 512; degradation | **Drop 512; the list is 32/64/128/256, default 256.** Budget: worst case ≤ 40 % of one core at 48 k/128, typical factory preset ≤ 12 %. The projection from the parent's measured 17.29 % at 128 grains is about 34 % at 256 and about 62 %+ at 512. Degradation is deterministic. In steady state each (voice, stream) onset clock is **thinned** to its water-filled quota, so grains are never truncated under sustained overload. Stealing (with a fade into spare slots) happens only at quota transitions and voice steals. Cap lowering converges. | §9, §11, Risks |
| D4 | Per-voice source → global destination | **Newest sounding voice** (last-triggered voice that is still gated or releasing). Its value is held when no voice sounds, with a 20 ms handover ramp. The matrix UI marks such routes "mono". Loudest-voice was rejected because it flips between voices at near-equal levels. Disallowing was rejected because it kills velocity→reverb, pressure→feedback and similar routes. | §20 |
| D5 | Dorico microtonal note expression in v1 | **Yes.** It is cheap here: the module already serves 10+ plugins, the JUCE patch marker is present in the pinned tree, and per-grain pitch is latched at spawn, so a per-note cents offset is one add. It is implemented with MPE in Phase 2.5 and DAW-verified in Stage 4 (COMPAT-02). The module's `VST3Extensions` is subclassed so the same object also returns `getPluginHasMainInput() = false` (the sidechain becomes `kAux`). | §2, §1 |
| D6 | Missing / unrouted AU sidechain for Record-in | **Signal presence decides, never bus state.** The bus state is only a prerequisite. With no bus, Record-in is disabled and the UI says "Sidechain unavailable in this host". With a bus present, a capture whose peak stays below −90 dBFS is **discarded, not committed**, and the UI says "No sidechain signal". Threshold trigger needs signal by construction. The input bus is never mixed to the output: the output channels are cleared before rendering. | §22, §1 |
| D7 | Feedback into working copies | **Per-slot record head at exactly 1× inside the stream's loop region, convex write `wc ← (1−λ)·wc + λ·r`, λ = 0.95·feedback.** Write-before-read per 32-sample pass, with the return delayed 32 samples (parent rule). The tap is the amp-env-weighted **mean** of that stream's voice clouds (÷ max(1, Σaₖ)), so loop gain never grows with voice count. There is one feedback chain per stream. Freeze = the record heads stop (the chains keep running, warm, discarded). Reset = an off-thread rebuild from pristine, then a 20 ms dual-read crossfade swap. Feedback 0 = no writes (bit-identical to pristine). | §17, Algorithm §3 |

## Core Components

### 1. Bus / I/O Adapter
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::AudioProcessor` (`BusesProperties` in the constructor), `juce::VST3ClientExtensions::getPluginHasMainInput()` (verified: `juce_audio_plugin_client_VST3.cpp:3108-3112`, `juce_VST3ClientExtensions.h:139`)
- **Purpose:** Stereo instrument output, plus one optional stereo **Sidechain** input for Record-in.
- **Parameters Affected:** none directly (`rec_*` read the input)
- **Configuration:**
  - `BusesProperties().withInput ("Sidechain", stereo, true).withOutput ("Output", stereo, true)`. The input is active by default because Logic only offers its Side Chain menu for an active bus (O-Comp precedent, memory `critical_au_hands_unrouted_sidechain_silence`).
  - `isBusesLayoutSupported`: output stereo only. Input disabled, mono or stereo. Channel counts come from the **bus**, never `buffer.getNumChannels()`.
  - VST3: return `getPluginHasMainInput() == false` so the only input bus is typed `kAux` (a sidechain), not a main input. This is implemented in the same subclass as the note-expression extensions (D5).
  - **The output is cleared before rendering.** JUCE hands an in-place buffer whose first channels hold the sidechain audio, so a synth that accumulates into `buffer` would leak track audio to its output. Copy the sidechain into a fixed 32-sample scratch per piece first, then clear.
  - `juce8-critical-patterns.md` §4 warns that an input bus on an instrument can cause "missing input" errors. This is mitigated by the `kAux` typing, gated by pluginval at strictness 10 (Stage 1) and checked in the DAW pass (Risks).
  - `IS_SYNTH TRUE`, `NEEDS_MIDI_INPUT TRUE`. `setLatencySamples (0)` in `prepareToPlay`.

### 2. MIDI / MPE / Note-Expression Front End
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::MidiBuffer` iteration only. **Not** `juce::MPEInstrument` / `MPESynthesiser`: its `Array<MPENote>` `add`/`remove` reallocates (`minimiseStorageAfterRemoval`), and O-Contrabass documents "MPESynthesiser allocates per note-on". `Ouaricon::NoteExpression::VST3Extensions` (note-expression 1.1.1, header-only).
- **Purpose:** Turn MIDI into sample-stamped voice events and per-note expression values with zero allocation.
- **Parameters Affected:** `mpe_enable`, `pitch_bend_range`
- **Configuration:**
  - Fixed state: `chanBend[16]`, `chanPressure[16]`, `chanSlide[16]`, `rpnState[16]`, `memberBendRange[16]`, `polyAT[128]`, `modWheel` (CC1 with optional 14-bit CC33), `sustain` (CC64).
  - **MPE off:** channel bend × `pitch_bend_range` applies to all voices. Channel AT or poly AT (whichever the note last received) is the Pressure source. CC74 on any channel is Slide.
  - **MPE on (lower zone):** channel 1 is the master channel and channels 2–16 are member channels. A member channel's bend, pressure and CC74 drive only that note. Member bend range = the last RPN 0 received on member channels (default **48** per the MPE spec). The master channel uses `pitch_bend_range`. The MPE Configuration Message (RPN 6) is accepted for the lower zone only (an upper zone is v1.1).
  - **Note expression (VST3, D5):** `drainAndUpdate()` at the top of `processBlock`. `applyPendingTuning` gives a per-note cents offset that is latched into the voice at note-on and updated live. It adds to MPE bend. It correlates by `noteId`, never by pitch (module contract).
  - Output: an event list (fixed capacity 512 per block; overflow drops the latest and counts it in telemetry), sorted by sample offset with a stable tie order: note-off before note-on at the same offset.

### 3. Voice Allocator
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (fixed `std::array<Voice, 20>`). The steal policy is a port of `plugins/O-simpleWavetable/Source/WtSynthesiser.h` (oldest-first, protect the lowest and highest held notes, prefer released voices), not the JUCE Synthesiser: our render is grain-major on a 32-grid, not per-voice `renderNextBlock`.
- **Purpose:** Poly / Mono / Legato voice management with click-free stealing.
- **Parameters Affected:** `polyphony`, `voice_mode`, `glide`
- **Configuration:**
  - 20 slots = up to 16 counted voices + **4 steal spares**. A stolen voice is not counted. It gets a 5 ms forced release (amp env ramp to 0 from its current level), and its grains keep rendering under that ramp. The new note takes a free slot. If all 4 spares are still fading, the quietest one is ended (its env is already below −40 dB by then). This is the voice-level form of the move-to-spare-slot pattern.
  - A voice ends when its amp env finishes release (< −96 dB). Its remaining grains are then silent (env 0) and are released with no fade.
  - **Note serial:** a global note-on counter (`uint64`). All grain, scheduler and Note Random draws key on the serial, never on the voice slot, so steal or allocation order cannot change the random content.
  - Mono/Legato: a 128-entry fixed note stack, last-note priority. Mono retriggers the envelopes **from the current level** (no reset to 0). Legato does not retrigger on overlapping notes. Both glide.
  - Glide: linear in semitones over `glide` ms (constant time). In Poly mode with glide > 0, a new voice starts at the last played note's pitch.
  - Sustain pedal (CC64) holds the gate. A note-off received while sustained is applied on pedal-up.
  - Lowering `polyphony` while notes sound force-releases the oldest excess voices over 5 ms (no stuck notes, and the limit converges at once).

### 4. Per-Voice Envelopes (Amp + Mod ADSR ×2)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom. Not `juce::ADSR`: its linear segments and sample-count stage logic have known traps in the suite (memory index: ADSR traps), and we need a retrigger from the current level.
- **Purpose:** DSP-02 amp shaping; per-voice mod sources.
- **Parameters Affected:** `amp_attack/decay/sustain/release`, `vel_to_amp`, `menvN_*`
- **Configuration:**
  - Per-sample, analog-style exponential segments (RC toward an overshoot target, as in O-simpleSubtractive). Attack and release floors are **2 ms** (the 0 ms parameter floor still gets a de-click ramp, as required by the draft spec).
  - Envelope times are latched at stage entry. Changes apply to the next stage, so no rate steps occur mid-segment.
  - Velocity gain `g_v = (1 − d) + d·v²`, d = `vel_to_amp`.
  - The amp env output `aₖ[n] = env·g_v` is computed for the whole piece into a `float[20][32]` array. It is used by the mixer and by the feedback normaliser.

### 5. Slot Store and Loader (off-thread)
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::AudioFormatManager` (`registerBasicFormats`: WAV, AIFF, FLAC, Ogg, and MP3 where the platform reader allows), `juce::AudioFormatReader`, `juce::ThreadPool` (1 worker), `juce::CriticalSection` (off-audio only)
- **Purpose:** Decode, resample to the session rate, build the mip tape and waveform overview, all off the audio thread (PERF-03).
- **Parameters Affected:** none (plugin state)
- **Configuration:**
  - Job = (slot, source, generation). A newer job for the same slot cancels the older one (`shouldExit` checks).
  - Decode to float. Keep the **pristine** at its native rate (level 0, mono stays mono). Cap the length at `30 s` of source. Longer files load their first 30 s and the UI shows "trimmed".
  - Resample native → session rate with a custom offline **Kaiser-windowed sinc** (double precision, 32 zero-crossings per side, cutoff 0.95·min(fs_in, fs_out)/2, β ≈ 9). It runs off-thread, so the cost is irrelevant. `juce::WindowedSincInterpolator` was rejected because of its 0.990 DC gain (memory `critical_juce_windowedsinc_dc_gain_is_0990`), and Lagrange because it aliases. Mono is upmixed L=R at tape build.
  - Build the `MipTape<4>` (§7) by running the same sequential writer the record head uses, so a rebuilt tape and a live-written tape are filtered identically.
  - The overview is a peak pair per 512 frames (UI lanes).
  - `SlotInfo` (path, name, frames, rates, trimmed flag, overview, missing flag) is message-thread-owned under a `CriticalSection`. The audio thread never takes it. This is the O-TextureForge 1.6.2 / O-simpleSampler lock rule: `setStateInformation` and `prepareToPlay` run on host threads, so a bare shared pointer is a race (memory `pattern_texture_forge_swap_needs_lock_if_prepare_publishes`).
  - **Sample-rate change:** `prepareToPlay` queues a rebuild of every loaded slot from its pristine copy, via `callAsync` deduped by (slot, rate). It never decodes on the host thread. Until the new tape arrives, the reader multiplies the rate by `tapeRate/fs` (correct pitch), and that slot's record head is parked (no writes at a mismatched rate).

### 6. Slot Handoff (audio-owned swap + retire reaper)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom: `std::atomic<SlotTape*> pending[4]`, SPSC retire ring (capacity 16), `juce::Timer` reaper
- **Purpose:** Lock-free, allocation-free installation of a new tape (load, reset, record, SR rebuild) with no click (FUNC-02, QUAL-01).
- **Configuration:**
  - Publish (message thread): `old = pending[s].exchange (tape)`. If `old != nullptr`, the audio thread never saw it, so the message thread deletes it at once.
  - Take (audio thread, at a grid tick): `p = pending[s].exchange (nullptr)`. Only the audio thread ever retires a tape it has used. It pushes the tape to the retire ring **after** its fade is complete and no grain references it. The reaper timer (and a producer-side sweep in `publish`) deletes it on the message thread.
  - **Why this, not the +2-generation reaper:** retirement is produced *by the audio thread*, so nothing can be retired while the host idles the audio thread, and `pending` holds at most 1 tape per slot. That removes the unbounded-queue failure of the generation reaper (memory `pattern_generation_reaper_freezes_when_host_idles_audio_thread`) by construction.
  - **Same-geometry swap (Reset, SR rebuild):** 20 ms **dual-read crossfade**. Each grain on that stream reads both tapes and blends (2× read cost on one stream for 20 ms). The record head is parked during the fade.
  - **New file / recording:** the stream's live grains get the 5 ms kill fade (`Grain::killGain`). New spawns read the new tape at once. Voices keep playing; only grains cross the swap. This refines the BRIEF's "voices fade out across the swap".
  - The processor destructor deletes current, fading and pending tapes and drains the ring.

### 7. MipTape<4> (working copy with mip levels)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom. A positional (non-circular) sibling of grain-engine `MipRing`/`MipSnapshot` that reuses `blr::halfband`, `kHbDelay`, `SincBank` and the `latchLevel`/`setFor` contracts from `BandlimitedReader.h`. It is a module-gap candidate: **G5** `MipTape` → grain-engine 1.2.0.
- **Purpose:** The per-slot working copy. Band-limited positional reads at any rate up to 16 (DSP-07), plus sequential incremental writes from the record head.
- **Configuration:**
  - **L = 4.** The final per-grain pitch is clamped to **±48 st** (rate ≤ 16), so `latchLevel ≤ 4` and the residual r′ ∈ [1, 2) gives sinc sets S0–S6 (≤ −60 dB). A key above root + 48 holds that pitch (documented). The parent uses L = 2 at ±24 st; at rates ≤ 4 `latchLevel` picks the same level, so parity holds (DSP-01).
  - Storage: level l has `ceil(F/2^l)` frames × 2 ch float. Total 1.9375 × level 0.
  - `writeRun (pos, n, L[], R[])`: writes level 0, then updates level l at index `(p − 63·(2^l − 1)) / 2^l` from the 127 most recent level-(l−1) samples read from the tape itself. This is the same group-delay compensation as `MipRing`, so a pitched read of a written region equals a `MipRing` read of the same audio. Levels settle `delayOf(l) = 63·(2^l − 1)` samples behind the write position. The record-head read guard covers that (§10).
  - `readStereo (level, pos, set, l, r)`: positional, absolute **double** frame position (memory: float read positions lose the fraction from about 12 s), with mirrored edges at the array ends.
  - Loop wrap: when the record head jumps from `loopEnd` to `loopStart`, the level filters see old content before `loopStart` for ≤ 63·(2^l − 1) samples. This affects only pitched reads in that sliver, and is accepted.

### 8. Scan Playheads
- **JUCE Class:** Custom
- **Purpose:** FUNC-04: where in the loop region each cloud reads.
- **Parameters Affected:** `sN_position`, `sN_scan_rate`, `sN_scan_mode`, `sN_loop_start`, `sN_loop_end`
- **Configuration:**
  - Loop region `[lo, hi) = sort(loop_start, loop_end) · F` (ordered in the DSP; no parameter writes), with a minimum width of 10 ms.
  - Scan offset σ (tape frames, double) advances by `scanRate · tapeRate/fs` per sample.
    - **Retrigger:** one σ per (voice, stream), set to 0 at note-on.
    - **Free-run:** one σ per stream, shared by every voice. It runs continuously and resets in `prepareToPlay`.
    - **Ping-pong:** per voice, retriggered like Retrigger, and reflects at the region edges.
  - Read centre `c = lo + wrap (position·W + σ, W)`, with `W = hi − lo`. Position is modulatable and moves the centre directly.
  - Scan 100 % moves 1 tape-second per output second (FUNC-04 criterion). Scan 0 holds still.

### 9. Voice × Stream Schedulers (×80)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom wrapper over `ouaricon::grain::GrainScheduler`. It is the parent's `StreamScheduler` with a voice dimension (telescoping jitter, Tempo grid lock; GR-ARCH §4 and §17).
- **Parameters Affected:** `sN_enable`, `sN_density`, `sN_density_sync`, `sN_jitter`, `sync_mode`
- **Configuration:**
  - A scheduler runs only for (sounding voice) × (enabled stream). The first onset lands exactly at the note-on sample (frac 0).
  - **Onset thinning (D3):** the interval is `fs / density` × `max(1, N_kS / q_kS)`. Here `N_kS = density·len_s` is the nominal overlap, and `q_kS` is the water-filled quota (§11). Under sustained overload, clouds get sparser rather than having their grains truncated. Both values are parameter-derived and computed at the grid, so this is deterministic and block-size invariant.
  - Draw keys: `Draw (seed, kSchedStream + s, (serial << 24) | onsetIndex)`.
  - Tempo mode: the onset grid is shared by all voices (onsets on the host grid). Thinning in Tempo mode skips whole grid divisions (power-of-two), as in the parent's density modulation.

### 10. Grain Spawner
- **JUCE Class:** Custom. A fork of the parent `Spawner.h` (GR-ARCH §5), rewritten for positional reads and the voice dimension.
- **Purpose:** Turn an onset into a fully latched grain.
- **Parameters Affected:** every grain-class `sN_` parameter (the per-voice modulated value at the spawn sample), `sN_root_note`, `sN_root_fine`, `sN_key_track`, `pitch_bend_range`
- **Configuration:**
  - Draw before obtain (memory). Fixed CounterRng slots (the parent's `Slot` enum, append-only) on `kGrainStream + s`, counter `(serial << 24) | onsetIndex`.
  - **Pitch (semitones):** `st = keyTrack·(note + glideOffset + bend + neCents/100 − root − rootFine/100) + sN_pitch + mod + Q(pitchRand·(2u−1))`. Q is the parent `ScaleQuantiser` in interval mode, counted from unison. The key term is never quantised (BRIEF). The result is clamped to **±48**, and the rate is `exp2(st/12) · tapeRate/fs` in double. At the root with keyTrack 100 %, the rate is exactly 1 (FUNC-03 ±1 cent holds by construction).
  - Length `len = size·(1 + sizeRand·(2u−1)·0.5)`, clamped to [5, 2000] ms.
  - **Start position:** `p₀ = c + spray·W·(u − ½)`. Then the **region fit**: reflect p₀ into `[lo, hi − reach]` with `reach = rate·len` (forward) or into `[lo + reach, hi)` (reverse), so a grain never crosses the loop seam. When `reach ≥ W` the read wraps inside the region (documented: a non-seamless loop is audible there, as in any sampler).
  - **Record-head clamp (only while that slot's head is writing):** in head-relative coordinates `d = p − h` (mod W), a forward grain at rate r sweeps `d₀ + (r − 1)·t`, and a reverse grain sweeps `d₀ − (r + 1)·t`, for t ∈ [0, len]. The forbidden d₀ interval is the one whose sweep crosses 0, widened by `margin(level)` on the behind side (unsettled mip levels) and by 16 frames on the ahead side. If p₀ falls in it, move it to the nearer feasible edge. If `|slope|·len + guards ≥ W`, no feasible start exists, so accept the crossing (the splice step is λ·|r − wc|, which is small at low feedback). This is the parent's reach clamp (GR-ARCH §5), generalised to a moving head in a loop.
  - Level and sinc set are latched (`latchLevel (rate, 4)`, `SincBank::setFor`). Reverse with `u < reverseProb` (0 % and 100 % exact).
  - Per-grain FX, window step, skew, pan and gain are latched exactly as in the parent (GR-ARCH §8–§9).
  - New `Grain` fields: `voice` (slot index), `serial`, `tape` (the tape pointer latched at spawn, used during the dual-read crossfade and for kill-on-swap).

### 11. Shared Grain Pool + Voice×Stream Quotas
- **JUCE Class:** Custom: `ouaricon::grain::GrainPool<Grain, 256, 32>` (grain-engine 1.1.0) + forked `Quotas.h`
- **Purpose:** One preallocated pool for all voices and streams (PERF-01/02).
- **Parameters Affected:** `grain_limit` (32/64/128/256), all density/size parameters
- **Configuration:**
  - The water-fill (parent `waterFill`, generalised from 4 to 80 demands) runs over the nominal demands `N_kS` of active (voice, stream) pairs with capacity `grain_limit`. It runs at grid rate from latched parameters, never from occupancy.
  - Steady state: thinning (§9) keeps the live count ≈ Σq ≤ cap, so the pool rarely fills.
  - **Transitions** (a new note shrinks the others' quotas, `grain_limit` is lowered, or voices steal): `obtain(progress)` with priority `progress(g) = 4·stolenVoice + 2·overQuota(k,s) + (k,s == spawning) + age·invLen`. Victims move to the 32 fade spares (5 ms). Steal-free renders stay bitwise unaffected (memory `pattern_grain_steal_fade_move_to_spare_slot`).
  - **Cap lowered live converges** (memory `pattern_cap_lowered_live_never_converges`, parent D25): while `alive > cap`, each acquire also kill-fades one more over-quota victim. Thinning also stops over-quota spawning, so the count reaches the cap within one grain length. Gate GL3-style: "lowered live under over-demand", with a no-converge control hook.
  - Live counts are for flags and telemetry only. They never enter a gain law.

### 12. Grain Renderer
- **JUCE Class:** Custom over `MipTape<4>::readStereo` + WindowMorphBank
- **Purpose:** Per grain per sample: band-limited positional read → per-grain FX → window × gain × pan → (voice, stream) bus.
- **Configuration:** As GR-ARCH §7: grain-major per render segment, window applied **last**, double `readAbs += step`. Buses are `float[20][4][2][32]` (fixed size, immune to oversized host blocks). During a slot's dual-read crossfade, the read is `(1−w)·old + w·new` for that stream's grains.

### 13. Window Morph Bank (forked verbatim)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (parent `WindowMorphBank.h`, grain-engine `WindowLut` underneath)
- **Parameters Affected:** `sN_window`, `sN_window_skew`
- **Configuration:** Unchanged (GR-ARCH §8): 65 tables × 2048, per-half-window μ₁/μ₂, latched at spawn.

### 14. Per-Grain FX (forked verbatim)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom POD inside `Grain` (parent `GrainFx.h`). Not `juce::dsp::StateVariableTPTFilter` or `IIR::Filter`: 256 instances with ProcessSpec overhead, and the `IIR::Filter` default constructor is first-order and allocates (memory, critical).
- **Parameters Affected:** `sN_filter_type/cutoff/rand/res`, `sN_drive`, `sN_crush`, `sN_crush_prob`, `sN_ring_freq/rand/mix`
- **Configuration:** Unchanged (GR-ARCH §9). The SVF and ring ceilings stay at 0.45·fs (Nyquist clamp, not 20 kHz).

### 15. Level Laws (forked `OutputLaw.h`)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom
- **Purpose:** Each (voice, stream) cloud is level-flat across density, size and window (DSP-01 parity), and the feedback tap is bounded.
- **Configuration:**
  - Effective overlap per (k,s): `N_eff = min(N_kS, q_kS)` with **full** windows. Thinning means no grain is truncated in steady state, so the cap-truncated-window moment from memory `pattern_grain_density_norm_over_cap_truncates_window` only applies to transient steals and is not part of the steady-state law. Output `g_out = 1/sqrt(max(1, N_eff·μ₂(m,skew)/μ₂_Hann))` with the parent's coherence blend (GR-ARCH §10). Feedback tap `g_fb = 1/max(1, N_eff·μ₁(m,skew))` (coherent, always).
  - Gains are computed per (k,s) at the grid and ramped over one cell. Quota changes at note events therefore glide, never step.

### 16. Voice-Stream Mixer
- **JUCE Class:** Custom
- **Parameters Affected:** `sN_level`, `sN_pan` (per voice: the per-voice modulated value), `sN_mute`, `sN_solo`, `sN_enable`
- **Configuration:**
  - Per sample: `out_s += aₖ[n] · g_out,kS · level_kS · pan_kS · bus_kS`. Mute/solo/enable gains ramp over 10 ms per stream (additive solo, no listener writes; GR-ARCH §11).
  - Fixed voice headroom **kVoiceGainDb = −6 dB**, tunable at the 2.2 listening pass. Polyphony sums are not normalised (an instrument gets louder with chords), and the wet safety knee (§18) bounds the peak.
  - Feedback tap per stream: `tap_s[n] = Σₖ aₖ[n]·min(level_kS, 1)·audible_s·g_fb,kS·bus_kS[n] / max(1, Σₖ aₖ[n])`, an amp-weighted **mean** of the voice clouds (D7).

### 17. Working-Copy Feedback Network (×4 chains + record heads)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom: 4 × forked `FeedbackChain` (TPT HP/LP, 4-allpass diffuser mix, `tanh(dx)/d`, AGC 0.7, NaN scrub; GR-ARCH §12) + per-slot `RecordHead`
- **Purpose:** DSP-04: grain output is written back into each stream's own working copy. It also covers Freeze, Reset and the runaway guard.
- **Parameters Affected:** `feedback`, `fb_low_cut`, `fb_high_cut`, `fb_saturation`, `fb_diffusion`, `freeze`; actions Reset (all / per slot)
- **Configuration:**
  - **One chain per stream**, all four driven by the global fb parameters. Stream s feeds only slot s. Cross-feeding between slots is out of scope for v1 (it would put one slot's material into another slot whose root note no longer describes it).
  - Chain input = `tap_s` (unity knob gain). Output `r_s` goes to a 32-sample return delay.
  - **Record head** `h_s`: advances exactly 1 tape frame per output sample (the tape is at session rate) and wraps in the stream's loop region (latched at each wrap).
    - `writing_s = !freeze && λ_s > 0 && tapeRate == fs && !swapFading_s && (stream has a sounding voice || returnEnv_s > −100 dBFS)`.
    - Otherwise it is **parked**. A parked head means the copy keeps its evolved state between phrases ("the instrument remembers").
  - Write: `wc[h] ← (1 − λ)·wc[h] + λ·r[n − 32]`, with `λ = 0.95·feedback`, ramped. Each write is a convex combination of bounded signals, so the copy cannot grow (Algorithm §3).
  - Feedback 0 means λ = 0, so there are no writes and the copy stays bitwise pristine (DSP-01 parity).
  - **Freeze:** heads stop. The chains keep computing on the grain output (warm state) and their return is discarded (parent rule).
  - **Reset:** an off-thread rebuild of that slot's tape from pristine, installed by the same-geometry dual-read swap (§6). Reset while frozen restores pristine and stays frozen.

### 18. Output Reverb + Wet Safety + Output Gain
- **JUCE Class:** `ReverbUnit` (reverb-unit 1.2.0, atomic bind; `juce_dsp`)
- **Parameters Affected:** `reverb_mix/size/damp`, `output_gain`
- **Configuration:** As the parent (GR-ARCH §13–14) minus dry/wet: there is no dry path. Wet safety `1.9953·tanh(x/1.9953)` (the parent's D9 knee: identity ≤ −6 dBFS, asymptote +6 dBFS), then `output_gain`.

### 19. Modulation Sources
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (forked `ModSources.h` LFO core; grain-engine `CounterRng`)
- **Parameters Affected:** `lfoN_*` (incl. `lfoN_mode`), `macroN`, `menvN_*`
- **Configuration:**
  - **Global LFO:** unchanged (parent hybrid phase: free clock or ppq phase in Tempo; S&H/smooth via `hash(cycle)`).
  - **Per-voice LFO:** one phase accumulator per voice, reset to `lfoN_phase` at note-on. Rate is modulatable per voice. Its S&H draws key on `(serial, cycle)`.
  - Mod Env 1–2: §4. Velocity (unipolar), Key `(note − 60)/64` clamped to [−1, 1] (bipolar), Note Random `CounterRng (seed, kNoteStream, serial)` (unipolar), Pressure (unipolar), **Slide bipolar `(cc74 − 64)/64`** (so a neutral controller adds nothing), Bend bipolar (per note, normalised by its range), Mod Wheel (unipolar, global), Macros (unipolar, global).
  - All sources are sampled once per 32-sample cell (per voice where applicable).

### 20. Control Grid + Modulation Matrix
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (forked `ControlGrid.h` + `ModMatrix.h` slot/ramp/shadow logic; GR-ARCH §16)
- **Parameters Affected:** `modM_source/dest/depth` (M = 1–16), all destinations
- **Configuration:**
  - Absolute 32-sample grid. Normalised-space evaluation `range.convertFrom0to1 (clamp (base01 + Σ depth·src, 0, 1))`. 20 ms slot ramps and route-change shadow crossfade (including the parent's 3.3 D36 route-edit fix if it lands; see the fork rule in §A1).
  - **Destination classes:** *per-voice* (all `sN_` destinations, plus `lfoN_rate` when that LFO is Per-voice) and *global* (`output_gain`, feedback ×5, reverb ×3, `lfoN_rate` when Global).
  - **Evaluation:** global-source routes are summed once. Per-voice-source routes are summed per sounding voice into a sparse per-voice offset vector (≤ 16 routes × ≤ 20 voices per cell).
  - **Per-voice source → global destination (D4):** uses the **newest sounding voice's** source value. A newer note takes over with a 20 ms ramp. If no voice sounds, the last value is held. The UI marks these routes "mono".
  - Per-grain-class destinations are read at the spawn sample (latched). Ramped destinations (`level`, `pan`, fb, reverb, output) interpolate within each cell. The engine **never** writes APVTS. Destination values for the UI are published as `std::atomic<float>`: global destinations directly, per-voice ones from the newest voice.
  - **New append-only destination table** of 126 entries (draft). Pin it with a golden ID-order test in Stage 1.

### 21. Transport / Tempo Tracker (forked)
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::AudioPlayHead::PositionInfo` (Optional getters); parent `TempoTracker.h`
- **Purpose:** Tempo density/size divisions, LFO sync, `rec_length_sync`.
- **Configuration:** Unchanged (GR-ARCH §17). It is shared by all voices.

### 22. Record-In Capture
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (a preallocated stereo capture buffer of `F_max(fs)` frames, sized in `prepareToPlay`)
- **Purpose:** FUNC-07: capture the sidechain into a target slot.
- **Parameters Affected:** `rec_target`, `rec_arm`, `rec_trigger`, `rec_threshold`, `rec_length`, `rec_length_sync`, `rec_gain`, `sync_mode`
- **Configuration:**
  - The run state (Idle → Armed → Recording → Committing) is engine state, published to the UI as an atomic. It is never a parameter.
  - **Start:**
    - Manual: the `rec_arm` rising edge.
    - Threshold: the first sample where the peak of `|sc·recGain|` exceeds `rec_threshold`.
    - Next Note: the next note-on offset.
    - Sample-accurate in every case.
  - **Stop:** when the length is reached (seconds, or bars × host bar length while Tempo is active and playing; capped at `F_max`), or on the `rec_arm` falling edge (partials ≥ 0.5 s are committed).
  - **Commit:** the audio thread sets `captureReady (frames)`. The message thread copies out, builds the tape (pristine = the capture at fs; no resample), publishes it through §6 to `rec_target`, and writes a 32-bit float WAV to `userMusicDirectory/Ouaricon/O-GranulatorInstrument/Recordings/` on the worker thread. Until the copy-out completes, a new Armed state waits (the buffer is busy). The copy never involves the audio thread, so a host that idles the audio thread is harmless.
  - **Degradation (D6):** see the D6 row and System Architecture → Record-In Availability.
  - Record-in does not drive mod sources (out of scope v1).

## Processing Chain

```
                     Sidechain bus (kAux) ─► copy to scratch ─► [rec_gain] ─► Record-in capture ─► (commit: message thread → tape build → slot swap)
                                             │ output buffer CLEARED here (never pass input through)
MIDI ─► MIDI/MPE/NE front end ─► voice events (sample-stamped) ─► Voice allocator (20 slots: ≤16 + 4 steal spares)
                                                                     │ per voice: amp env aₖ[n], mod envs, glide, per-voice LFOs, MIDI sources
                                                                     ▼
 Control grid (32-smp, absolute) ─► sources ─► matrix (global + per-voice offsets; newest-voice rule for global dests) ─► quotas (water-fill 80 demands)
                                                                     │
   Slot s tape (MipTape<4>, session rate) ◄── record head h_s: wc ← (1−λ)wc + λ·r_s[n−32]   (writes first in every piece)
        │ positional band-limited reads (double pos)                                      ▲
        ▼                                                                                  │
   Voice k × Stream s schedulers (thinned to q_kS) ─► spawner (region fit, head clamp, pitch = key-track + offsets, ±48 st)
        ▼                                                                                  │
   GrainPool<256 + 32 fade> ─► per grain: read → SVF → drive → crush → ring → window·gain·pan ─► bus[k][s]
        ▼                                                                                  │
   Voice-stream mixer: out_s += aₖ·g_out·level·pan·bus  ;  tap_s = Σ aₖ·g_fb·bus / max(1, Σaₖ)
        │                                                   └─► FeedbackChain_s: HP → LP → diffuser mix → tanh(dx)/d → AGC → scrub → z^-32 ─┘
        ▼
   Σ streams (mute/solo/enable ramps) ─► ReverbUnit ─► wet safety 1.9953·tanh(x/1.9953) ─► output_gain ─► Out (stereo)
```

**Per-piece order (normative).** The host block is cut at every absolute multiple of 32 samples. Each piece `[a, b)` (≤ 32 samples) runs:

1. At a grid point: control tick (params, ramps, sources, matrix, quotas, laws, transport, take `pending` tapes).
2. Apply the MIDI events in `[a, b)` at their offsets (voice start/stop/steal, gate edges, expression). Compute `aₖ[n]` and the mod envs for the piece.
3. Sidechain → scratch → capture (if recording). Then clear the output range.
4. **Record-head writes** for n ∈ [a, b): `r_s[n − 32]` comes from earlier pieces (`kCell ≤ kFbDelay`, static_assert).
5. Schedule every active (voice, stream) over `[a, b)` → onsets, merged by (offset, serial, stream). This is an explicit tie-break (memory: sort ties change the RNG assignment).
6. Render grain-major in segments split at onsets → `bus[k][s]`. Every read position lies outside the head's unwritten-this-pass region (spawner clamp).
7. Mixer → stream sums + `tap_s`. Then feedback chains → `r_s` into the return delays (computed even while frozen).
8. Reverb → wet safety → output gain → `out[a, b)`. Telemetry snapshot.

This is the parent's pass engine (GR-ARCH Processing Chain) with a voice dimension and positional tapes. It is bit-identical across block sizes, every scratch array is a fixed 32 samples, and an oversized host block cannot overrun anything (memory `pattern_oversampler_overruns_on_oversized_host_block`; there is no oversampler here).

---

## System Architecture

### MIDI Routing
- `acceptsMidi() = true`, `producesMidi() = false`. MIDI channel handling, MPE and note expression are as in §2. No MIDI output.
- Events are sample-accurate: applied at their offsets inside the 32-grid pieces, never snapped to block or cell starts.

### File I/O and Sources
- **User files:** drag-drop through `modules/core/webview-drop-streaming` (macOS WKWebView strips paths; the module streams content into a session temp dir and calls a loader callback) and a `juce::FileChooser` browser. Formats: WAV/AIFF/FLAC (+ Ogg/MP3 where JUCE's readers allow). "Slots may share a file" means each slot decodes its own copy. Memory is per slot, so sharing is a UI convenience only.
- **Factory sources:** embedded as **BinaryData FLAC** in a second `juce_add_binary_data` target, referenced as `factory:<id>`. This is the suite precedent (O-simpleGrain `embedded:<name>`). It removes the installer/content-folder dependency from the BRIEF. Budget ≤ 8 MB, 6–8 licence-clean sources. Watch the two juce_add_binary_data traps: hyphen stripping and the dual `BinaryData` namespace collision with the UI target (memory index: build notes).
- **Recordings:** saved as 32-bit float WAV under `userMusicDirectory/Ouaricon/O-GranulatorInstrument/Recordings/` and referenced by path. Embedding is on by default for recordings (they exist on one machine only).

### State Persistence
- **APVTS:** all parameters (incl. the 48 matrix params).
- **ValueTree `<Engine>`** (parent keys, unchanged): `seed` (**int64**; memory: `getLargeIntValue` clamps uint64 > INT64_MAX), `stateVersion`, `modDestTableVersion = 1`, `customScale.*`, `degreeMasks[4][32]`, `uiLanguage`.
- **`<Slots>` (new, per slot):** `source` (`factory:<id>` | `file:<abs path>` | `rec:<abs path>` | empty), `name`, `fileSize`, `contentHash` (xxHash64 of the first 1 MB of decoded PCM, used for relink matching), `rootNoteHint` (none in v1), `embed` (bool, opt-in), `embedded` (base64 FLAC-24, only if `embed` and the encoded size is ≤ **16 MB**), `trimmed`. The working-copy state is **not saved**: on reload it restarts from pristine.
- **Resolve order on load:** absolute path (exists and size matches) → embedded blob → filename + hash search in the Recordings folder → `factory:` → **missing** (slot empty, UI "relink", plugin stable; FUNC-06).
- `setStateInformation` can run on a host thread. It only parses and enqueues loader jobs (§5). It never decodes inline, and it never touches audio-owned tapes.
- **Presets:** preset-manager (Stage 4) with the known traps: reset to defaults before apply, the stale `<CustomState>` child fix, never set `output_gain`. Factory presets reference `factory:` sources only.

### Record-In Availability (D6)
| Host condition | Detection | Behaviour |
|----------------|-----------|-----------|
| No input bus (layout disabled / 0 ch) | `getBus(true,0)` null, disabled, or 0 ch | `rec_arm` is ignored. UI: "Sidechain unavailable in this host". No error, no noise. |
| Bus present, nothing routed (AU hands silence) | Signal presence: running peak during Armed/Recording | Threshold never fires. Manual/Next-Note captures run, but a capture with peak < −90 dBFS is **discarded** with the UI note "No sidechain signal". The slot is unchanged. |
| Bus present, routed | Peak above −90 dBFS | Normal capture. |
| VST3 host routes track audio into the aux input | — | It is captured only when armed. Input is never passed to the output (it is cleared). |

The memory note (`critical_au_hands_unrouted_sidechain_silence`) is honoured: bus state is a prerequisite only; signal presence decides. No one-way latch is needed, because each capture is judged on its own content.

### Threading Model
- **Audio thread:** everything in the Processing Chain. No locks, no allocation, no logging, no file I/O. `ScopedNoDenormals` per block.
- **Worker thread (1, `juce::ThreadPool`):** decode, resample, tape build, overview, WAV write, FLAC encode for embedding.
- **Message thread:** APVTS/UI, `SlotInfo` (under a lock that only off-audio threads take), publish to `pending`, the reaper timer, capture copy-out, `callAsync` SR-rebuild dedupe.
- **Host threads** (`prepareToPlay`, `setStateInformation`, `getStateInformation`): only touch `SlotInfo` under its lock and enqueue jobs.
- **Parameter listeners never write other parameters** (VST3 nested-write trap). Actions (Load, Relink, Clear, Reset, Save recording) are native functions, not parameters.

### Telemetry (UI-01 / UI-02 feeds)
- Grain snapshot: up to 288 entries `{voice, stream, normPos, gain, reversed}` per frame in a triple buffer (parent `UiTelemetry.h`).
- Per slot: the record-head position, an evolving overview (peaks updated on the write path, ≤ 1 bin per cell), and the swap/reset state.
- Per voice: note, amp level and scan centre per stream (playheads in the lanes, keyboard / voice-activity indicator).
- The 126 modulated destination values (global destinations, plus per-voice ones from the newest voice) and the 17 source values (per-voice ones from the newest voice).
- Record-in state, sidechain peak (max since last read), output peak (max since last read; parent D38 definition).

## Algorithm Details

### 1. Read/write ordering (load-bearing)
Per-piece order above. Invariants (debug asserts + gates):
- `passLen ≤ kFbDelay = kCell = 32` (static_assert, parent).
- While a head writes, no grain's read interval over its life contains a frame within `margin(level)` behind or 16 frames ahead of the head, unless the region is too short (counted in telemetry as `forcedCrossings`).
- RNG draws are pure functions of (seed, stream, serial, onsetIndex, slot).
- **Gate:** a seeded render with a scripted MIDI chord sequence (incl. steals, sustain, bend, MPE pressure), every randomisation on, feedback 80 %, freeze toggles and LFO/per-voice routes, at host blocks 32/441/512/4096/variable, must be bit-identical (`max|Δ| == 0`). A different-seed control must differ (memory `pattern_grain_read_before_capture_write_blocksize`; large-block probe included).

### 2. Pitch and key tracking (FUNC-03, DSP-07)
`st = κ·(note + g + b + ne/100 − root − fine/100) + p + m + Q(ρ·(2u − 1))`, clamped to ±48. `rate = exp2(st/12)·tapeRate/fs` (double).
- At note = root, κ = 1, all offsets 0: rate = 1 exactly (×1.0 when tapeRate == fs), so the ±1 cent criterion holds by construction.
- κ = 0: the key term vanishes, giving a fixed pitch for every key.
- A 44.1 k file in a 96 k session is resampled to 96 k at load, so the rate is exact. Before an SR rebuild lands, the `tapeRate/fs` factor keeps the pitch exact.
- Aliasing at +24 st: level 2 + S0–S6 ≥ 60 dB (grain-engine B-tests). Gate: +24 and +48 st swept sine, aliases ≥ 60 dB down.

### 3. Working-copy feedback: stability argument (DSP-04)
Let `‖·‖` be the peak bound of a slot's content.
- The tap is the weighted mean `Σ aₖ yₖ / max(1, Σ aₖ)`, so its bound is the max over voices of the single-cloud bound. A single cloud with the coherent law `g_fb` has a small-signal gain of ≤ 1 relative to the tape content. Each voice's level contribution is capped at unity (`min(level, 1)`).
- The chain is HP/LP (gain ≤ 1, Butterworth k ≥ √2), then a diffuser **mix** (|(1−m) + m·e^{jφ}| ≤ 1), then `tanh(dx)/d` (≤ 1 small-signal; |out| ≤ 1/d ≤ 1), then AGC (peak ≤ 0.7).
- The write `wc' = (1−λ)wc + λr` with λ ≤ 0.95 is a convex combination. So `‖wc'‖ ≤ max(‖wc‖, ‖r‖) ≤ max(‖wc‖, 0.7)`. The copy never exceeds its pristine peak or 0.7, for **any** voice count and any feedback setting. That is DSP-04 criterion 1 by construction, before the wet safety knee.
- **Known consequence:** a mean (not an incoherent sum) darkens the written layer by about 3 dB per voice doubling for uncorrelated chord voices. It is accepted because it is safe for coherent unisons (MPE duplicates, same-key voices). The fallback is `1/sqrt(Σa)` with a coherence guard, but only if hands-on finds chords too thin in the copy.
- NaN scrub on the return and on the grain SVF state. A non-finite write is replaced by the old `wc[h]`.
- **Gates:** 60 s, 16 voices held, feedback 100 %, density 200, size 500 ms, pitch +12, all streams +6 dB, res 100 %: the tape peak never exceeds max(pristine peak, 0.7), output ≤ +6 dBFS, no NaN/Inf/denormal. Freeze: the tape hash is unchanged over 10 s of play. Reset: the tape hash equals the pristine build. Feedback 0: the tape hash equals pristine after 60 s of play.

### 4. Record-head clamp (§10) closed form
For a forward grain, `s = r`. The relative sweep is `Δ = (r − 1)·len`. The forbidden `d₀ ∈ [min(0, −Δ) − g_b, max(0, −Δ) + g_a]`, with `g_b = margin(level)` and `g_a = 16`. For a reverse grain, `Δ = −(r + 1)·len`, same formula. The interval is taken mod W. Choose the feasible d₀ nearest the drawn one; ties go to the "behind head" side (fresh content). Infeasible when `|Δ| + g_a + g_b ≥ W`. A parked head means no constraint.

### 5. Onset thinning + quotas (D3)
`N_kS = density_kS·len_kS/fs` (nominal overlap). Water-fill over the active pairs gives `q_kS`. The interval multiplier is `max(1, N_kS/q_kS)`. In Tempo mode the multiplier is rounded **up** to a power of two, so onsets stay on the grid. `N_eff = min(N, q)`, giving the level law in §15. The multiplier changes only at grid ticks; the scheduler re-times via the parent wrapper (`sinceOnset` tracking, module gap G3 optional).

### 6. Per-grain FX, window morph, scale quantiser
Verbatim from the parent (GR-ARCH Algorithm §5 interval mode, §9). The absolute-follow mode and `scale_root` are removed.

## Integration Points

### Feature Dependencies
```
MIDI/MPE/NE ─► Voice allocator ─► per-voice env/sources ─┐
Control grid ─► matrix (global + per-voice) ─► quotas ───┼─► Schedulers(k,s) ─► Spawner ─► Pool ─► Renderer ─► Mixer ─┬─► Reverb ─► Out
Transport ─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        ▲              ▲                                  │
Loader (worker) ─► pending ─► Slot handoff ─► MipTape ◄── record head ◄── FB chain_s ◄── tap_s ◄───────────────────┘
Sidechain ─► Record-in ─► (message thread) ─► Loader
```

### Parameter Interactions
- `feedback` × `freeze`: frozen means no writes. Feedback still shapes nothing audible until unfrozen.
- `sN_loop_start/end` × record head × spawner: the region bounds the reads, the head wrap and the head clamp. A short region makes forced crossings more likely (telemetry).
- `sN_density` × `sN_size` × `polyphony` × `grain_limit` → quotas → thinning → `N_eff` → both laws.
- `sN_root_note/fine` × `sN_key_track` × bend / MPE / NE → rate. The ±48 clamp applies after `sN_pitch`, mod and spread.
- `voice_mode` Mono/Legato × `sN_scan_mode` Retrigger: Legato does not retrigger the scan (no new note-on event for the voice). Mono does.
- `mpe_enable` × `pitch_bend_range`: see Design Sync S2.
- `sync_mode`: picks `rec_length` vs `rec_length_sync`, size/density/LFO sync params (no parameter writes).

### Processing Order Requirements
MIDI before scheduling; record-head writes before reads; schedule before render; spawns in (offset, serial, stream) order; mixer before the feedback chains; reverb outside the loop.

### Thread Boundaries
Audio thread ↔ message/worker only via `pending[4]` (exchange), the retire SPSC ring, the capture `ready` atomic and telemetry atomics/triple buffer. No shared pointers are touched on the audio thread.

---

## Implementation Risks

### CPU (PERF-02): HIGH
- **Model** (from parent measurements, not estimates): C7 worst = 17.29 % of one core at 128 grains (all FX, feedback, reverb, MPM), 48 k/128, M-series. That is about 0.11 % per grain at the worst FX config.
- Projection at 256: ≈ 28 % grains + 4 chains (~2 %) + reverb (~1.5 %) + 20 voices of envs, matrix and 80 schedulers (~2–3 %) ≈ **34 %**. At 512 the projection is **≈ 62 %+** (124 % at 96 k), so 512 is rejected (D3).
- **Budget:** worst case (16 voices × 4 streams saturating 256, all FX, feedback 100 % on 4 chains, reverb) ≤ **40 %** of one core at 48 k/128. Typical factory preset ≤ **12 %**. Measured as a ratio against an engine-bypass baseline, with a machine-speed calibration witness (parent 2.6 finding: a shared core reads as FAIL, not NOVERDICT).
- **Levers, in order:**
  1. Hermite reads for rate ≤ 1 at level 0 (gate the timbre).
  2. 4-lane SIMD over same-(k,s) grains.
  3. Skip FX stages via latched `active` flags (already in).
- **Fallback:** default `grain_limit` 128 plus a documented "heavy" warning in the UI above 128.

### Feedback into working copies (DSP-04): HIGH (novel)
- Risks: splices when a grain crosses the head (mitigated by the §10 clamp); pitched-up cascades piling HF into the tape; the convex mean making chords thin.
- **Fallbacks:**
  - (a) Splices audible even with the clamp: write through a 2 ms raised-cosine "brush" on the leading edge at head start/stop (no change to steady writes).
  - (b) HF build-up: a fixed −1.5 dB/oct tilt above 8 kHz in the chain (parent fallback).
  - (c) Musical failure of the 1× loop-region head (evolution too slow on long regions): a v1.1 "Follow" write mode, where the head laps a window around the newest voice's read footprint. This needs one Choice param, so it is not in v1.

### MipTape incremental mips: MEDIUM
New structure. Gate: a tape built by `writeRun` over a region must be **bit-identical** to a `MipRing` fed the same samples, at every level, inside settled indices (offset by the group delay). Pitched read of a written region vs `MipSnapshot` of the same audio: ≤ −120 dB.

### File load / swap / reaper (PERF-03, QUAL-01): MEDIUM
Covered by the audio-owned swap (§6). Gates:
- An allocation gate across load, reset, record commit, SR change and steal (malloc_logger, thread-scoped).
- A swap click gate on a tonal source vs a no-swap control.
- A host-idle test: publish 100 loads with `processBlock` not called; memory is bounded at ≤ 1 pending per slot.
- A `prepareToPlay`-stress test (O-TextureForge `prepare_stress.cpp` pattern).

### Instrument + sidechain bus (COMPAT-01, QUAL-02): MEDIUM
`juce8-critical-patterns.md` §4 records "missing input" errors when an input bus is added to an instrument. Mitigation: `kAux` typing (VST3), active-by-default for Logic, pluginval 10 on both formats in Stage 1, and the Logic / Live / Reaper DAW pass in Stage 4. **Fallback:** ship VST3 without the input bus (Record-in AU/Standalone only) via a format-conditional `BusesProperties`. QUAL-02 is `nice`, so this does not block v1.

### MPE / note expression: LOW-MEDIUM
A custom parser (no JUCE MPE classes). The NE module is proven in 10+ plugins. Gate: per-note bend on 3 held member-channel notes moves only its own voice; RPN 0 sets the member range; NE −50 ¢ on C#4 plays a quarter-sharp C4.

### Block-size invariance with MIDI + 80 schedulers: MEDIUM
Every known class (read-before-write, RNG interleave keyed by serial, block-relative scheduling, sort ties, accumulated ppq) is closed structurally by the absolute 32-grid. The null gate (Algorithm §1) catches regressions.

### Fork drift: MEDIUM
O-Granulator 3.3 is still allowed a DSP touch (D36 route-edit fix). Mitigation in Architecture Decisions §A1.

### Memory: LOW
Lazy, per loaded length (see Special Considerations).

### Overall Project Risk
HIGH complexity, MEDIUM technical risk. About 60 % of the DSP is forked, proven parent code. The genuinely new work is the voice dimension (allocator, per-voice matrix, quotas over 80 pairs, thinning), MipTape plus record-head writes and the clamp, the slot loader/swap, Record-in, the MPE parser, and state/relink.

---

## Architecture Decisions

### A1. Fork-now at leaf level, converge later (D1)
- **Why not a shared module now:**
  - The parent is mid Stage 3, under an "audio must not move" constraint (CONTEXT-3.3: carried diffs byte-identical).
  - Its leaf APIs can still change (D36 may touch ModMatrix).
  - Its `Engine` is not reusable: it has one live ring, delay-based reads, one loop, the MPM/onset analysis and global streams.
  - Extracting a module mid-phase would force O-Granulator re-gates for no benefit to it.
- **Why not a whole-engine fork:** about 40 % of the engine (CaptureWriter, Analysis, write arbiter, freeze head-stop, pitch follow) does not apply, and the voice dimension touches every remaining orchestration file.
- **Plan:**
  1. At Phase 2.1 start, copy the leaves (`GrainFx.h`, `WindowMorphBank.h`, `OutputLaw.h`, `Quotas.h`, `ScaleQuantiser.h`, `FeedbackChain.h`, `TempoTracker.h`, `ControlGrid.h`, `Grain.h`, `EngineConstants.h` subset, `ModSources.h` LFO core, `ModMatrix.h` slot logic, `UiTelemetry.h`) into `Source/dsp/forked/`. Rename the namespace from `ogran` to `ogi` to avoid ODR clashes in shared test binaries.
  2. Write `Source/dsp/forked/FORK-MANIFEST.md`: source path, source commit (the commit that closes O-Granulator 3.3, at least `3043b72a`), sha256 at copy, and a list of local modifications per file.
  3. Every Stage-2 verify runs a drift check: parent sha256 vs manifest. A changed parent file gets a **hunk-by-hunk diff review** (memory `pattern_fork_review_drift_label_can_hide_local_fix`) and an explicit take/skip entry.
  4. After O-Granulator Stage 4 ships, promote GrainFx, WindowMorphBank (G1), OutputLaw, Quotas, FeedbackChain and MipTape (G5) into **grain-engine 1.2.0**, then converge both plugins under each plugin's block-size null plus digest gates (`/converge-modules`).

### A2. Positional tape at session rate + native pristine (D2)
- Writes are 1:1 with output samples (no fractional write resampler), and reads use the parent's reader contracts.
- Keeping pristine at native rate makes Reset and SR changes disk-free.
- **Rejected:** reading at native rate with a rate factor (needs a fractional-rate band-limited writer for feedback); pristine at session rate with mips (+64 % memory for a copy used only by Reset).

### A3. Convex write, mean tap, per-stream loops (D7)
- The stability bound is a one-line argument independent of voice count, versus the parent's additive "input + fb" ring, which needs the full four-layer analysis.
- It matches the BRIEF's "the copy drifts; Reset restores" semantics. Under re-injection Reset would be almost redundant.
- Feedback 0 is a bitwise no-op.
- **Rejected:**
  - Re-injection `wc = pristine + fb`: the copy heals itself lap by lap, so Reset loses its meaning.
  - Additive overdub: unbounded without decay.
  - A head at the scan position: static at the default scan 0, and per-voice in Retrigger.

### A4. Thinning instead of steady-state stealing (D3)
- With 16 voices the over-demand can be 50× the cap. Steal-oldest would then run tens of thousands of steals per second, beyond any spare-slot budget, and truncate every grain into an attack-only click texture.
- Thinning keeps grain shape and gives a closed-form level law (full windows). The stealing path stays for transitions.

### A5. Newest-voice rule (D4)
- Deterministic, matches the "last key" convention of polyphonic synths (e.g. Reason Thor's monophonic "Last Key" source), stable, and keeps per-voice expressions useful on global FX.

### A6. Custom voice allocator, custom MPE parser
- JUCE `Synthesiser` mallocs on steal in 8.0.15 (memory, critical), and the per-voice `renderNextBlock` model fights the 32-grid grain-major engine.
- `MPEInstrument`'s `Array<MPENote>` reallocates on add/remove.

### A7. Factory sources embedded (BinaryData), not a content folder
- Suite precedent (O-simpleGrain). No installer changes, and presets always resolve.

---

## Special Considerations

### Thread Safety
Audio-thread-only engine state. Tapes are handed off via atomics only. `SlotInfo` is under a lock taken only by non-audio threads. No APVTS writes from the audio thread or from listeners. Allocation happens in `prepareToPlay` (pool, buses, capture buffer, chains, morph bank, reverb), on the worker (tapes) and on the message thread (copy-out).

### Performance
Fixed 32-sample scratch everywhere. Per-(k,s) buses `20×4×2×32` floats (20 KB). Grain POD ≈ 230 B × 288 slots ≈ 66 KB (L2-resident). Water-fill over ≤ 80 demands per cell (insertion sort of the active set only).

### Memory (D2)
| | 48 k session | 96 k session | 192 k session |
|---|---|---|---|
| Slot max | 30 s | 30 s | 15 s (2.88 M-frame cap) |
| Working tape per full slot (×1.9375 mips, stereo float) | 22.3 MB | 44.6 MB | 44.6 MB |
| Pristine per full slot (native 48 k stereo float) | 11.5 MB | 11.5 MB | 11.5 MB (15 s → 5.8 MB) |
| 4 full slots | ≈ 135 MB | ≈ 225 MB | ≈ 200 MB |
| + in-flight (1 tape build + capture buffer) | + 34 MB | + 67 MB | + 67 MB |

Typical use (4 × 8 s sources at 48 k) ≈ 36 MB. Allocation follows the loaded length. `prepareToPlay` allocates only the capture buffer (`F_max·2·4 B`).

### Denormal Protection
`ScopedNoDenormals` per block; FTZ covers the SVFs, AGC envelopes, diffuser, reverb and the env tails. NaN scrubs on the loop return, the grain SVF and the tape write. Envelopes end at −96 dB (no subnormal tails). Custom ramps reset to the target explicitly (memory: `SmoothedValue::reset` does not clear a NaN).

### Sample Rate Handling
44.1–192 kHz. Tapes are rebuilt from pristine on an SR change (off-thread), with `tapeRate/fs` rate correction and parked heads until they land. Filters clamp to 0.45·fs. The diffuser and reverb scale with fs. Slot length is capped in frames.

### Latency
**0** (`setLatencySamples (0)` in `prepareToPlay`). Note-on to first grain: 0 samples (the first onset fires at the event offset). The feedback return delay of 32 samples is internal to the loop.

## Research References

### Professional Plugins
- **Ableton Granulator III** (Robert Henke): 12-voice polyphony plus a mono mode. Cloud mode allows up to 20 grains per channel per note. MPE pressure/slide per note. Capture records live input into the instrument and **replaces the loaded sample with parameters unchanged**. This validates Record-in → slot replace, a fixed modest polyphony, and per-note MPE on grain parameters.
- **Arturia Pigments** sample/granular engine: user reports put 256 polyphonic grains near the practical ceiling ("16 voices … high density with long size grains will choke"), with grain limit and polyphony as the CPU levers. This validates the 256 cap and the user-facing `grain_limit`.
- **Mutable Instruments Clouds / Beads:** feedback into the recording buffer, freeze = stop writing, parameters read once per grain. This validates latch-at-spawn and freeze semantics.
- **Reason Thor:** "Last Key" monophonic source alongside per-voice MIDI key. This is the precedent for the newest-voice rule (D4).
- **Logic Pro EVOC 20 PolySynth / AU side-chain lore:** Logic routes the sidechain to an instrument's input bus. Developer reports conflict on which bus index, so this needs a DAW pass (Stage 4).

### Internal References
- `plugins/O-Granulator` @ 3043b72a: `research/ARCHITECTURE.md` (GR-ARCH), `Source/dsp/*` (fork leaves), VERIFICATION-2.1…2.6 (CPU C1–C7), CONTEXT-3.3 D34–D41.
- `modules/synthesis/grain-engine` 1.1.0 (`BandlimitedReader.h`: MipRing/MipSnapshot/SincBank, margins 9/80/222/506/1074; `GrainPool.h`; `CounterRng.h`; `GrainScheduler.h`).
- `plugins/O-simpleWavetable/Source/WtSynthesiser.h` (steal policy port), `plugins/O-Contrabass/Source/OContrabassMPESynthesiser.h` (MPE pitfalls: shouldStealVoices default, legacy mode, per-note allocation).
- `plugins/O-MicrotonalSampler/Source/RetiredMapReaper.h` (SPSC audio→message retire ring), `plugins/O-TextureForge` 1.6.2 (corpus lock, prepare race), `plugins/O-simpleSampler` (raw-ptr handoff + lock).
- `plugins/O-simpleGrain` 2.0.1 (embedded sources, FLAC state embedding, `kMaxRetainedSourceBytes`, polyphonic granular precedent).
- `modules/tuning/note-expression` 1.1.1 README (drain/correlate by noteId), `modules/core/webview-drop-streaming` 1.0.0.

### JUCE (local 8.0.15 headers)
